response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT team_id, CAST(SUM(w) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT year) AS avg_wins, AVG(CASE WHEN l <> 0 THEN CAST(g - l AS REAL) / l END) AS avg_ratio FROM manager_half GROUP BY team_id), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS mean_wins FROM t) SELECT t.team_id, t.avg_wins, t.avg_ratio, t.avg_wins - m.mean_wins AS gap FROM t CROSS JOIN m WHERE t.avg_wins > m.mean_wins ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Average wins per season = SUM(w) / COUNT(DISTINCT year) per team_id, summed across all managers and halves of that team in manager_half.
The mean of all teams' average wins is the unweighted mean across teams (each team counted once) computed from per-team averages.
(g - l) / l is undefined when l = 0 (division by zero), so such rows are treated as missing and ignored in the average (NULL via CASE).
Gap is avg_wins minus the overall mean; since only teams above the mean are kept, the gap is never missing, so the 'missing last' ordering has no effect.
